A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 37-page work, including Appendices A-F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical research content; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v1 reports original NORMAD-ETI experiments with seven LLMs and 21 model pairs, including accuracy, cultural parity, ablations and case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including single-model and debate accuracies in Tables 1-2, cultural parity in Table 3, and supplementary experiments in the appendices.

M1.justification: The Debate-Only and Self-Reflect+Debate procedures, feedback exchange, self-reflection choices and judge adjudication are identical. Section 3 and the Appendix A prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same NORMAD-ETI social-etiquette classification task across 75 countries. Dataset composition, cultural groups and label coverage remain unchanged, including Table 19.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: constant-label, single-model, self-reflection and oracle baselines, judge candidates, and the random/oracle adjudication comparisons in Appendix D are all retained.

E3.justification: Model configurations, prompts, accuracy and parity metrics, sampling temperatures, and debate/reflection iteration settings are identical, including the protocols for appendix experiments.

E4.justification: Both retain identical debate-round and reflection-iteration studies, decision-dynamics analyses, judge ablations, efficiency comparisons and case studies in Appendices C-F.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same p < 0.05 significance statement. Appendix C.5 and Table 9 still report averages over two runs with reversed option order; statistical reporting and run counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical tables, plotted results and case-study outcomes match throughout. For example, Table 2 retains final mean accuracies of 76.3% for Debate-Only and 75.6% for Self-Reflect+Debate.

T1.justification: The debate formulations in Equations 1-3, cultural-group parity definition in Equation 4, and oracle upper-bound reasoning are identical. No mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about improved accuracy and cultural parity, complementary LLM capabilities, and small debating models achieving accuracy comparable to a larger model.

C2.justification: Interpretations of complementarity, decision revisions and judge effects are unchanged. Section 8 retains the same limitations concerning dataset scope, generalization, ternary labels, debate variants, computational overhead and inference variability.

D1.justification: Appendix A prompts, Table 4 model identifiers, sampling details and Appendix E hardware/timing information are unchanged. The code/data release statement and repository link also match.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical, including positioning relative to CulturePark and earlier multi-agent debate research. No cited work or substantive novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 30 May 2025 to v2, 1 Sep 2025. The title, authors, prose, section order and appendix organization are identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions and their placement match throughout, including the appendices. The only visible difference is the version/date text recorded under P1; the document layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 reproduces the same methods, results, analyses, limitations and Appendices A-F as v1. The administrative version/date update does not meaningfully affect scientific support, reproducibility or clarity.
